newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lhasa Brewery to list A shares Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Lhasa Brewery to list A shares Wednesday.

text.p: China's Lhasa Brewery Co Ltd said on Monday it will list 22.5 million domestic currency A shares on southern China's Shenzhen exchange on June 25.

The company, based in the Tibetan capital of Lhasa, completed an initial public offering of 25 million A shares at 3.38 yuan each earlier this month. The issue was 18.6 times oversubscribed, the firm said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The firm's staff held 2.5 million A shares, which will not be listed until the other A shares are listed for six months, the statement said.
The company will use proceeds from the offer to expand production and market share in the remote Himalayan region, a share prospectus has said.
Most of the funds will be used to expand beer production capacity to 50,000 tonnes a year from the current 35,000 tonnes over the next 18 months, the prospectus said.

It said the rest of the money would be invested in building a production line for beer cans to replace glass bottles, which break too easily in the freezing temperatures that often hit the lofty Tibetan plateau.
As the region's sole brewery, the company expects to boost its market share in Tibet to 50 percent from 30 percent, helped by increasing demand, it said.
Lhasa Brewery posted a net profit of 15.20 million yuan for 1996 and 2.93 million yuan for 1995.

Despite the earnings surge, the firm's profits were capped by an invasion of beers made in other regions of China and poor road conditions in the largely undeveloped region that made long-distance delivery difficult, the company said.
Lhasa Brewery has 66 million shares outstanding, composed of 41 million shares held by state institutions and 25 million A shares.
